bytes_declared_note: CMR granule_size; LOWER bound — real day files are declared ~100 B

grid.col_order: col 0 is 180 W (centre -179.9): the producer's 0.1 .. 359.9 E columns ROTATED by W/2, a lossless permutation; the pixels are the producer's own
grid.coordinates: lon = x0 + (col + 0.5) * dx, lat = y0 + (row + 0.5) * dy; x0/y0 are the grid's WEST and SOUTH edges
grid.extent_note: [west, south, east, north] in degrees; +-40 latitude
grid.no_tile_corners: a plain geographic grid: the affine rule above IS the lat/lon of every pixel and tile corner
grid.row_order: row 0 is the SOUTHERNMOST row (bin centre -39.9) — the order of the L3 file's ascending `lat`

qc_policy: The PRODUCER's QC is inherited, not redone: an L3 hourly bin is the inverse-variance mean of the L2 samples the producer kept (fatal_composite_mss clear). A day-cell combines the hours whose value is finite, whose uncertainty is finite and > 0 and whose sample count is > 0 — per quantity, so the wind and the MSS keep their own valid hours; an hour that has a value but cannot be weighted is excluded and counted (`hours_*_unweightable`). Values outside the channel bounds (mss and its uncertainty in [0, 1], n_mss in [1, 2048], wind in [0, 99] m/s) become NaN and are counted, never clipped. A file that will not open or whose axes do not match the declared grid is `ctx.note_absent`, never a smaller frame. No independent-wind filter and no rain or slick mask is applied: those are the confounders the consumer must model (cygnss_mss_measure.json, `confounders`).
